I am a research technician for both the Miles and Buczkowski labs. I grew up moving all over the U.S., which instilled in me a great fascination with wildlife and natural systems. I have a broad general background in urban ecology and IPM, and my research focuses on the effects of habitat fragmentation on ant ecology. Prior to working in the Miles lab, I got both my Undergraduate and master's degrees at Purdue university. My master's thesis involved studying agriculturally isolated forest fragments through the lens of island biogeography, using ants as a model organism.
